title: Factorization of a reflected square mate through its ambient mate
statement:
For $W\in\{S,T,X,Y\}$ let $\mathcal A_W$ be a category with a full reflective subcategory $\mathcal C_W$, reflector $C_W$ and unit $\kappa_W$; precomposition by $\kappa_{W,M}$ is a bijection on Hom into every object of $\mathcal C_W$. Suppose four adjunctions $L_f\dashv R_f$, $L_g\dashv R_g$, $L_h\dashv R_h$, $L_e\dashv R_e$ have directions $L_f:\mathcal A_S\to\mathcal A_X$, $L_g:\mathcal A_S\to\mathcal A_T$, $L_h:\mathcal A_X\to\mathcal A_Y$, $L_e:\mathcal A_T\to\mathcal A_Y$, and each right adjoint preserves the full subcategories. Identify each reflector with an endofunctor through the full inclusion. For $L_u:\mathcal A_a\to\mathcal A_b$, set $P_u=C_bL_u|_{\mathcal C_a}:\mathcal C_a\to\mathcal C_b$, $D_u=R_u|_{\mathcal C_b}:\mathcal C_b\to\mathcal C_a$ and $k_{u,M}=\kappa_{b,L_uM}:L_uM\to P_uM$. Thus $P_f=C_XL_f|$, $P_g=C_TL_g|$, and $P_h=C_YL_h|$, $P_e=C_YL_e|$. Equip $P_u\dashv D_u$ with the specified Hom bijection sending $t:P_uM\to N$ to the ordinary adjunct of $t\circ k_{u,M}$. Products of morphisms below mean composition, with the rightmost morphism applied first. Suppose $\theta:L_hL_f\xrightarrow{\sim}L_eL_g$ and $\theta^c:P_hP_f\xrightarrow{\sim}P_eP_g$ are natural and satisfy, for $M\in\mathcal C_S$,
$$\theta^c_M k_{h,P_fM}L_h(k_{f,M})=k_{e,P_gM}L_e(k_{g,M})\theta_M.$$
For $K\in\mathcal C_T$ let $b_K:L_fR_gK\to R_hL_eK$ be the ordinary mate of $\theta$, and let $\alpha_K:P_fD_gK\to D_hP_eK$ be the completed mate of $\theta^c$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Then
$$\alpha_K k_{f,D_gK}=R_h(k_{e,K})b_K.$$
This equation is natural in $K$ and uniquely determines $\alpha_K$ among maps $P_fD_gK\to D_hP_eK$. Equivalently the ordinary $L_h\dashv R_h$ transpose of $\alpha_K k_{f,D_gK}:L_fR_gK\to R_hP_eK$ is $k_{e,K}L_e(\varepsilon_{g,K})\theta_{R_gK}$. The target $R_hP_eK$ lies in $\mathcal C_X$, so the uniqueness uses the reflector Hom bijection at $L_fR_gK$. No assertion that either mate is invertible is included.

proof.text: Fix $K\in\mathcal C_T$ and put $M=D_gK=R_gK\in\mathcal C_S$, $N=P_eK\in\mathcal C_Y$. Write $H_u$ for the ordinary adjunction Hom bijection and $\Phi_u(t)=H_u(tk_{u,-})$ for the specified reflected bijection. Let $\delta_K=\varepsilon^c_{g,K}:P_gM\to K$. Since $\Phi_g(\delta_K)=\mathrm{id}_{D_gK}$, we have $H_g(\delta_K k_{g,M})=\mathrm{id}_{R_gK}=H_g(\varepsilon_{g,K})$. Injectivity gives $\delta_K k_{g,M}=\varepsilon_{g,K}$. This uses only the definitions of counit and of $\Phi_g$; $K\in\mathcal C_T$ is exactly the target hypothesis of the reflector bijection.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change: mate defined by its counit transpose; the reflector calculation is supplied by the agent from the stated Hom bijections.

proof.text: Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] to the two reflected adjunctions $P_g\dashv D_g$ and $P_h\dashv D_h$, with intervening functors $P_f,P_e$ and transformation $\theta^c$. Its transpose description says that the reflected transpose of $\alpha_K$ is $\psi_K=P_e(\delta_K)\theta^c_M:P_hP_fM\to N$; equivalently $\Phi_h(\psi_K)=\alpha_K$. The required four functor directions are precisely those in the statement.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change: mate defined by its counit transpose; the reflector calculation is supplied by the agent from the stated Hom bijections.

proof.text:
Define the ordinary inverse Hom bijection by $T_h(a)=\varepsilon_{h,N}L_h(a)$ for $a:B\to R_hN$. The specified formula for $\Phi_h$ in step 1 and step 2 give $T_h(\alpha_K)=\psi_K k_{h,P_fM}$. Functoriality then gives
$$T_h(\alpha_K k_{f,M})=\varepsilon_{h,N}L_h(\alpha_K)L_h(k_{f,M})=\psi_K k_{h,P_fM}L_h(k_{f,M}).$$
Here $P_fM\in\mathcal C_X$ and $N\in\mathcal C_Y$, so the reflected Hom formula applies.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change: mate defined by its counit transpose; the reflector calculation is supplied by the agent from the stated Hom bijections.

proof.text:
Substitute $\psi_K$ from step 2 and apply the assumed square compatibility at $M\in\mathcal C_S$. The expression in step 3 becomes
$$P_e(\delta_K)\theta^c_M k_{h,P_fM}L_h(k_{f,M})=P_e(\delta_K)k_{e,P_gM}L_e(k_{g,M})\theta_M.$$
This is substitution of the hypothesis; it requires no invertibility of a completion unit.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change: mate defined by its counit transpose; the reflector calculation is supplied by the agent from the stated Hom bijections.

proof.text:
Naturality of $\kappa_Y$ at $L_e(\delta_K)$ is
$$P_e(\delta_K)k_{e,P_gM}=k_{e,K}L_e(\delta_K).$$
Indeed $\delta_K:P_gM\to K$ has both endpoints in $\mathcal C_T$, and $P_e$ is $C_YL_e$ on that full subcategory. Applying this to step 4, functoriality and step 1 give
$$T_h(\alpha_K k_{f,M})=k_{e,K}L_e(\delta_K k_{g,M})\theta_M=k_{e,K}L_e(\varepsilon_{g,K})\theta_{R_gK}.$$

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change: mate defined by its counit transpose; the reflector calculation is supplied by the agent from the stated Hom bijections.

proof.text:
For the ordinary mate, [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives $T_h(b_K)=L_e(\varepsilon_{g,K})\theta_{R_gK}$, now with target $L_eK$. Counit naturality at $k_{e,K}:L_eK\to P_eK$ yields
$$\varepsilon_{h,P_eK}L_hR_h(k_{e,K})=k_{e,K}\varepsilon_{h,L_eK}.$$
Consequently
$$T_h(R_h(k_{e,K})b_K)=k_{e,K}T_h(b_K)=k_{e,K}L_e(\varepsilon_{g,K})\theta_{R_gK}.$$
Steps 3-5 give the identical transpose for $\alpha_K k_{f,M}$. Injectivity of the ordinary inverse Hom bijection proves $\alpha_K k_{f,D_gK}=R_h(k_{e,K})b_K$ and the asserted transpose formula.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change: mate defined by its counit transpose; the reflector calculation is supplied by the agent from the stated Hom bijections.

proof.text: The object $P_eK$ is in $\mathcal C_Y$ by construction and $R_h$ preserves the full subcategories, so $R_hP_eK\in\mathcal C_X$. If $a,a':P_fD_gK\to R_hP_eK$ both satisfy the displayed factorization, then $a k_{f,D_gK}=a' k_{f,D_gK}$. Injectivity of the assumed reflector Hom bijection at $L_fR_gK$ with target $R_hP_eK$ gives $a=a'$. Thus the equation uniquely determines the completed mate.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change: mate defined by its counit transpose; the reflector calculation is supplied by the agent from the stated Hom bijections.

proof.text:
By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], $b$ and $\alpha$ are natural transformations. Put $\tau_K=R_h(k_{e,K})b_K$. For $a:K\to K'$ in $\mathcal C_T$, naturality of $k_e$ and $b$ gives
$$R_hP_e(a)\tau_K=R_h(k_{e,K'})R_hL_e(a)b_K=\tau_{K'}L_fR_g(a).$$
Likewise naturality of $\alpha$ and $k_f$ gives
$$R_hP_e(a)\alpha_K k_{f,D_gK}=\alpha_{K'}P_fD_g(a)k_{f,D_gK}=\alpha_{K'}k_{f,D_gK'}L_fR_g(a).$$
Hence the factorization is an equality of natural transformations on $\mathcal C_T$. No step takes the inverse of $k$, $b$ or $\alpha$.
